reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the output contract, resource-level rubric, fresh-review framework, resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, the direct HTTP behavior finding, R4 maturity data, and the local R4/R6 StructureDefinition evidence. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only because the assigned artifact is `SubstanceSourceMaterial`, not `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `SubstanceSourceMaterial` was trial-use/FMM 0, so the stability burden is weak and broad production impact should not be presumed from the break alone. That lowers the case for preserving the standalone resource identity, but it does not erase the regulatory/source-provenance risk of losing detailed source-material facts.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes the standalone `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resource and only partially folds it into `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`, so a resource-level migration program is unavoidable; the main remaining standards concern is avoiding lossy or underspecified source-material detail migration.

reasoning.thesisMd: `SubstanceSourceMaterial` is not a same-resource R4-to-R6 evolution. R4 had a concrete standalone DomainResource, while the R6 package has no `SubstanceSourceMaterial` StructureDefinition and the closest successor is an optional `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` backbone. That makes old instances, generated resource classes, endpoint assumptions, and persistence models fail unless migrated.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is resource removal plus partial remodel. R4 source-material data included class, type, state, organism identifiers/names, parent substances, geography, development stage, fractions, taxonomy/author/hybrid details, and part locations. R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` keeps a much smaller set: type, genus, species, part, and countryOfOrigin. Implementers therefore need policy for embedding or distributing old facts across `SubstanceDefinition`, generic classification/relationship/name/note fields, extensions, or retained legacy records.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the old `resourceType` itself has no R6 target, preserving one old child path or relaxing one binding would not make R4 instances directly R6-valid. At this resource level, migration planning dominates compatibility leverage. Still, that is not the same as saying additional break prevention has no value: selected optional detail preservation, explicit computable maps, or clear successor guidance could materially reduce lossy expert-dependent migration even after accepting the broader resource redesign.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Retaining `SubstanceSourceMaterial` as a deprecated R6 resource or endpoint alias would be the broadest less-breaking design, but for an FMM 0 specialized resource it would carry a second substance model, duplicate validation/search/API surface, and likely indefinite conversion burden. A narrower and more compelling alternative is standards work on a loss-aware R4-to-R6 map or selected optional source-material detail slots under `SubstanceDefinition` for high-value provenance facts. Relaxing the R6 country binding to extensible would preserve more legacy codes, but it would also weaken computable country comparability for a field whose semantics are specifically country of origin.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct HTTP finding confirms that the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource endpoints, including `SubstanceSourceMaterial`. For this resource that is a concrete API-discoverability consequence, but it is derivative of the resource identity removal rather than an independent reason to change the resource-level conclusion. The 11 shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings may affect generic infrastructure during an R6 migration, but they are not scored as `SubstanceSourceMaterial`-specific breaks here.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's main conclusion: resource identity removal makes major migration unavoidable and the practical posture is `migration-program-dominates`. The important nuance is that this should not discount the `sourceMaterial` detail-model finding as mere churn; even with migration unavoidable and FMM 0, the lossy regulatory/provenance mapping gap remains standards-review-worthy.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The main uncertainty is not whether the R6 resource identity is absent; that evidence is strong. The uncertainty is the intended official successor mapping, because no local R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, StructureMap, or authoritative migration note was available, and country terminology expansion was not available locally.

findingConsiderations.title: SubstanceSourceMaterial was removed as a standalone R6 resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceSourceMaterial"` has no same-name R6 StructureDefinition, and generated models, validators, endpoints, searches, and persistence keyed by the old resource require migration or explicit legacy support.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 source-material detail model is only partially represented by R6 SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding defines the substantive migration shape after the resource identity break: the likely R6 successor is smaller and not lossless. Because R4 carried detailed biological, taxonomic, fraction, geography, parent-substance, and part-location facts, this is standards-review-worthy despite the low FMM and unavoidable resource migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Likely mapped countryOfOrigin now has a required country ValueSet binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This remains a real migration chore for legacy local, text-only, historical, or non-country jurisdiction codes, and country provenance can matter for plasma, herbal, or biologically derived substances. It does not drive the resource-level conclusion because the resource must already be remodeled and the stricter country binding has a plausible comparability rationale.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding includes `SubstanceSourceMaterial` and matters for clients or conformance tooling that infer supported resource routes from the base CapabilityStatement. For this resource it is derivative of the R6 resource removal, so it reinforces migration planning rather than changing the model-level judgment.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta-delete operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a high-risk shared `Resource` behavior change for generic metadata-management workflows, but the review scope rules keep shared `Resource` findings as context unless the assigned artifact is `Resource` itself. It should not be counted as a `SubstanceSourceMaterial`-specific reason for major migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search-parameter metadata change may affect generic clients during an R6 migration, but it is not specific to the removed substance source-material model and was not used to decide this resource's compatibility leverage.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Produce or confirm an official computable migration map from R4 `SubstanceSourceMaterial` to R6 `SubstanceDefinition`, including where each R4 source-material class/state, organism, parent-substance, geography, development-stage, fraction, taxonomy, hybrid, and part-location fact should land.

Revisit the `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` redesign for loss-prone provenance details: either add selected optional base fields for high-value legacy facts or publish explicit guidance that these facts intentionally move to other `SubstanceDefinition` structures or extensions.
Provide country-of-origin normalization guidance for R4 local/text/historical country representations before validating against the R6 required country ValueSet.

Document REST and CapabilityStatement transition expectations for removed substance-source resources so clients know whether there are no R6 endpoints, replacement endpoints, or implementation-specific legacy aliases.

caveats: No official cross-version StructureMap, ConceptMap, or migration guide was available in the local packages, so the `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` successor is inferred from local StructureDefinition evidence.
R4 FMM 0/trial-use status and specialized substance-regulatory scope mean prevalence is uncertain and likely lower than for mature clinical resources.
Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were considered only as migration context, not as resource-specific break drivers.
